topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic on cancer evolution and outlines the core learning objectives regarding mechanisms of development, Darwinian selection, and microenvironmental interactions.

topics.label: Genetic and Epigenetic Drivers of Clonal Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how tumors initiate and progress through natural selection acting on cells that acquire competitive fitness advantages via genetic mutations or epigenetic changes.

topics.label: Stem Cell Hierarchies and the Cell of Origin
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the role of tissue differentiation hierarchies and stemness in cancer development by investigating whether malignancies originate from tissue stem cells or committed progenitor cells.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and Inflammatory Influences on Tumor Growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how local inflammation, external promoters, and stromal cell interactions in the microenvironment are required to stimulate neoplastic transformation and sustain tumor viability.

topics.label: Techniques for Investigating Cancer Evolution and Spatial Biology
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the genomic sequencing, transcriptomic, and spatial profiling technologies used to map tumor heterogeneity and cell-microenvironment interactions.

topics.label: Multifactorial Framework of Cancer Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the lecture's concepts into a comprehensive evolutionary framework showing how genetic alterations, cell of origin, epigenetic plasticity, and microenvironmental conditions converge to drive cancer.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Next Session Preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing housekeeping and indicates the topic for the following lecture.
